data.name: Pashupati
data.long_meaning: The name Pashupati is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Pashu’ meaning animals and ‘Pat’ meaning master or protector. Pashupati is the Lord of all creatures and is considered as the protector and provider of all beings.
data.spiritual_meaning: Pashupati represents the divine aspect of nature and the power to protect and nurture all beings. It is a name that invokes the power of nature and the strength and wisdom of the Lord.
data.numerology_meaning: Pashupati is a name that is associated with the number 2 in numerology. The number 2 is associated with balance, harmony, and partnership. It suggests that the bearer of this name is someone who values cooperation, harmony, and balance in their life.

vedic_reference.note: Pashupati is a manifestation of Lord Shiva and is considered as the protector of all creatures.

data.cultural_impact: Pashupati holds a significant place in Indian mythology and is one of the most revered forms of Lord Shiva. His image as the protector of animals and all living creatures resonates with the Indian society's deep respect and compassion towards all forms of life. Pashupati is also considered the patron deity of Nepal and is worshipped extensively there. Numerous shrines and temples are dedicated to Pashupati across the Indian subcontinent and Nepal.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Pashupati signifies the divine power and love of Lord Shiva towards all his creation. It represents the idea that the divine is not only transcendental but also immanent and embodied in all beings. Pashupati's role as the protector and provider emphasizes the importance of taking care of all beings and living in harmony with nature. The name thus inspires a sense of humility, compassion, and awe towards the divine presence in all things.

historical_references.reference: Pashupati is an epithet of Lord Shiva, who is considered as the protector of all creatures in this universe. The name Pashupati consists of 'Pashu' meaning animals and 'Pat' or 'Pati' meaning lord, protector or master.
historical_references.context: The Rigveda, one of the oldest existing texts in the world, contains several references to Rudra-Pashupati, an early form of Lord Shiva, as the god of all animals and protector of the universe.

historical_references.reference: The Pashupatinath Temple in Nepal is one of the most sacred Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Pashupati. It is believed that the temple was initially built in the 16th century AD, but its origins are said to date back to the 4th century AD.
historical_references.time_period: Medieval India and present day Nepal, from around 1000 CE to present
historical_references.context: The temple is situated on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu. It is revered by both Hindus and Buddhists and is famous for its significance in the cremation rituals of Hindus.

trends: Hindu deity, Lord of all creatures, Shiva, is popularly known as Pashupati in Nepal and India.

modern_usage.modern_context: In the modern context, the name 'Pashupati' is widely used on various platforms such as social media, spiritual websites, and the tourism industry. On social media, many devotees and spiritual groups use the hashtag #Pashupati to share images, stories, and experiences related to this deity. Spiritual websites often have sections dedicated to Pashupati, providing information about his history, significance, and rituals. In the tourism industry, the name is prominently used for temples, festivals, and tours related to Lord Pashupati, attracting thousands of pilgrims every year.

name_in_real_life.story: Anita Pashupati from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of Pashupati - "Lord of All Creatures". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Pashupati represents the divine protector and preserver of all beings in the form of Lord Shiva, the God of animals and nature. It signifies the welfare and well-being of all creatures under His compassionate gaze.
